pr.body:
Phase 2 of #78: streamed weights are copied on the GPU's transfer queue, one weight ahead, so copying and computing overlap.

## Why

Since #79, a weight that does not fit VRAM is copied into one of two VRAM slots before its GEMM. That copy sat in the compute batch, and the full barrier between copy and GEMM serialized them: a prefill chunk took copy time plus compute time. With every layer on the GPU (Qwen3-14B Q8_0, chunk 512) that is ≈ 0.55 s of copies + 0.4 s of compute.

## Change (Vulkan backend only)

- **Transfer queue:** where the device has a transfer-only queue family (the copy engines; the RTX 2080 Ti has one, RADV and lavapipe do not), a second queue, two command buffers and two timeline semaphores.
- **One submission per streamed GEMM:** `vk_seq_cut`, a roll; the ring grows to 1024 command buffers, while the regular rolls keep their 64. The GEMM's submission waits on `tl_copy` for its slot's copy and signals `tl_comp` when done; the next copy into that slot waits on that.
- **Prefetch:** a chunk streams its weights in the same order every time. Each weight learns its successor (`geist_buffer.stream_next`), and that one is copied into the other slot while the current GEMM runs.
- **Sharing:** only the weights in host memory and the slots are shared between the two queue families; weights resident in VRAM stay exclusive.
- **Hygiene:** destroying a weight waits for the transfer queue and clears it from the slots and the learned order.
- **Fallback:** a failing transfer submit turns async off; the copies go back into the batch.
- **Default:** on. `GEIST_VK_STREAM_ASYNC=0` turns it off; a device without a transfer-only family never had it.

## Results (RTX 2080 Ti + Ryzen 9 9950X, Qwen3-14B Q8_0, chunk 512)

| configuration | prefill async off | **prefill async on** | decode | peak VRAM |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| every layer on the GPU (4.7 GB streamed) | 551–553 | **654–660** | 2.61 both | 10684 MiB both |
| split 26 + offload | 522–540 | **616–638** | unchanged | 10200 / 10201 MiB |

Runs 1517, 1518, 1523, interleaved; raw data in `benchmark/results/raw/stream-async-2026-10-20/`. The streamed part is now bound by the copy (≈ 8.6 GB/s).

## Correctness

- **GPU test suite:** green with async on by default, on the real card (run 1528). Linear parity, buffer and ops tests also pass with async forced.
- **Split 26 + offload:** identical with and without async (INT8 max |d| 0.201, 16/16 greedy, run 1522).
- **Out of memory in `test_layer_split_int`:** the test runs out of VRAM in later configurations in **both** modes. The cause is a pre-existing leak, filed as #121: the Vulkan weight registry never releases a model's weights. Not this change: peak VRAM in a one-model process is identical.

Also: `test_layer_split_int` prints both backends' error message on a failed split; `stream-async.yml` measures async off/on with peak VRAM.

Refs #78, #121

docs(offload): phase 2 results, BACKENDS variable, CHANGELOG (#78)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

vulkan: async streaming on by default; a destroyed weight leaves no trace in it (#78)

Runs 1517-1523 on the RTX 2080 Ti: prefill with streamed weights +19 %
(every layer on the GPU 546-553 -> 654-660 tok/s, split 26 + offload
522-540 -> 616-638), decode and peak VRAM unchanged (10684 / 10200 MiB
both ways). GEIST_VK_STREAM_ASYNC=0 keeps the copies in the batch; a
device without a transfer-only queue family never had async.

Destroying a weight buffer now waits for the transfer queue and clears
it from the learned order and the slots, so no copy or prediction names
a freed buffer.

vulkan: share only the weights in host memory and the slots with the transfer queue (#78)

Run 1517: with async on, every weight buffer was created
SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT, and the split-26 test sessions no longer fit
the card (all KV modes out of memory, INT8 fits without async). The
transfer queue only ever copies from a weight in host memory into a
slot; the weights resident in VRAM stay exclusive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

vulkan: stream spilled weights on the transfer queue, one weight ahead (#78 phase 2)

Prefill with streamed weights cost copy time plus compute time: the
copies sat in the compute batch, and each full barrier between a copy
and its GEMM serialized them (Qwen3-14B Q8_0: 0.55 s of copies + 0.4 s
of compute per 512-row chunk with every layer on the GPU; 550 tok/s).

With GEIST_VK_STREAM_ASYNC=1 (opt-in) and a transfer-only queue family
(the copy engines; the RTX 2080 Ti has one, RADV/lavapipe do not), the
backend copies into the two VRAM slots on that queue instead. Each
streamed GEMM becomes a compute submission of its own (vk_seq_cut, a
roll; the ring grows to 1024) that waits on a timeline semaphore for its
slot's copy and signals another when done, and the next copy into that
slot waits on that. A chunk streams its weights in the same order every
time, so each weight learns its successor (geist_buffer.stream_next) and
that one is copied into the other slot while the current GEMM runs. Weight
buffers and slots are shared by both queue families. A failing transfer
submit turns async off and the copies go back into the batch.

stream-async.yml measures it on the geist-vulkan box.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
